newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Court upholds death sentences for graft in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds death sentences for graft in Vietnam.

text.p: An appeal by defendants in Vietnam's biggest corruption case was turned down on Monday, with the Ho Chi Minh City appeals court confirming death sentences for four ringleaders and prison terms for 11 others.
"All the charges and sentences decided by the lower court have been left unchanged," an appeals court official said at the end of the seven-day hearing.
The most prominent defendant in the now-notorious case was Pham Huy Phuoc, former director of Tamexco -- a Ho Chi Minh City trading firm affiliated to the ruling Communist Party.
He was accused of siphoning off some $26 million of state money from the firm, using some of it to buy a swanky villa for his mistress and gambling away tens of thousands of dollars in one card game.
He will now face the firing squad along with two company executives and a state official.
Given a last chance to make a statement to the court, each of the 15 defendants who appealed said that they had not committed all the crimes of which they were accused.
In all, 20 people were sentenced in the lower court hearing in January, five of whom decided not to appeal.
The state prosecutor said during the hearing that he wanted further investigations to establish whether other individuals should be drawn into the net for their part in the case.
The southern newspaper Tuoi Tre said that although the original verdicts were just, the appeal process could serve to throw light on other, senior officials who may bear some responsibility.

The scandal, whose murky details were published in state- controlled newspapers for months in an apparent bid to underline the government's determination to tackle corruption, has sent shockwaves through the establishment.
As the Tamexco appeal entered its second day last week, two other business executives were arrested in Ho Chi Minh City for alleged involvement in a multi-million dollar bank loans scam.

Tang Minh Phung, director of a clothing-to-construction company named after himself, and Lien Khui Thin of trading firm EPCO were both charged with "taking advantage of confidence to appropriate citizens' and socialist property".
The two companies were among several which have come under scrutiny for their involvement in southern Vietnam's brief property market boom and subsequent bust.
Economists say the firms used influence and connections to secure multiple loans from commercial banks, many of which are now sitting on mountains of debt.

"It's clear that the Tamexco case, followed by EPCO and Minh Phung have exposed the banking system's problem, which needs to be thoroughly overcome to avoid the possibility of more serious catastrophe," economist Lam Vo Hoang wrote in Tuoi Tre on Monday.
